detail:
Every time, the liveness control was the only thing that caught it. Any lane writing oracle cases against the v3 EventStore should assert that every seeded record actually projected, BEFORE scoring any exclusion.

The three refusals, all silent from the test's point of view (the event is rejected at admission and query() simply returns fewer rows):
1. Readable tenant names. tenantIdSchema requires t_<ULID>; "tenant-northwind" from the oracle text fails the envelope schema. Every C25 exclusion assertion passed against an empty store.
2. post bodies missing entry_type (required by postBodySchema). The C25 chunk bait was never admitted, so A4 was vacuous.
3. human_ruling on a decision record. Admission reserves that class for record type ruling (class_not_allowed: "human_ruling is reserved for ruling records"), and rulingBodySchema is STRICT - summary/rationale/applicability_conditions are all rejected. C05's governing disposition never existed.

Related and worth knowing: rulingBodySchema.requirements is the machine-checkable home for applicability conditions ("instead of tokens parsed out of prose"). A draft that puts them in free text makes condition-matching depend on string parsing, which the contract already anticipated.

Also: a record scoped {repo: X} with no tenant does NOT match a query naming a tenant - scopeMatches is exact on identity components. Policy records (principal/membership) are therefore invisible to tenant-scoped queries. Correct, but surprising when counting rows.
summary: Vacuous-pass hazard confirmed THREE times while writing the oracle cases: exclusion assertions passed against records that were never admitted to the store
